label: verify-bm-lay-analogies

claims.claim: Pine-cone scale is two-layer, opens dry/closes wet, dead cones keep doing it, so no living process needed.
claims.source_says: when dead fallen dry cones are moved into a humid environment, they close and open again when dried, an experiment that may be repeated many times. (also: bilayered structure of the individual scales)
claims.note: Source states all parts; 'no living process needed' is a fair inference.

claims.claim: Ceiling kappa <= 1.5 x mismatch/h is Lean-checked (5 theorems, 0 errors, 0 sorryAx), visible in the 1863 bimetal formula with a = 1 + square >= 1, not new (Holstov 2015 plotted it).
claims.source_says: 1/R - 1/R0 = 3/(2a) * Δε/h (Villarceau, 1863); Holstov: the maximum value of the function remains constant at 1.5
claims.note: Wikipedia raw source and Holstov PDF match; Lean file has 5 theorems incl. bilayer_rules_out and no 'sorry' text; Lean run itself not repeated.

claims.claim: Formlabs 0.7% is a 24 h weight gain of a 1 cm cube for Flexible 80A and Elastic 50A V2, not equilibrium nor size change; Flexible 80A V2 gains +8% mass in a day by another method.
claims.source_says: Formlabs measures resistance to solvents by observing, measuring, and weighing printed cubes (originally 1 cm) ... for 24 hours. Flexible 80A V2 TDS: Deionized Water 1 day -26 +8% +3%
claims.note: Both rows show 0.7% water; TDS shows +8% mass at 1 day; 'not equilibrium' is inferred from the 24 h design.

claims.claim: Diffusion time scales as thickness squared ideally (4x), but pine-cone fits give exponents 1.5 (drying) and 1.3 (wetting), so half-thickness strips are 2.5 to 4 times faster.
claims.source_says: the shrinking (drying) time varies as τd = 96 h_a^1.5 min and the swelling (wetting) time varies as τd = 29 h_a^1.3 min (h_a in mm)

overall: All four key claims reproduce against the original sources (PMC2838359, Wikipedia raw formula, Holstov PDF, Formlabs page and TDS PDF); the Lean result was not re-run, only the theorem statements checked.
